messages.subject: rror: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'x' is not available or its output type is unknown.
parts:
Hello All,

I am having trouble with the compiling step of my nimble model. I keep getting this same error for one of my nimble functions, however after testing this function as an individual compiled C function it works as it should.

The main error message I keep getting is 
"Compiling [Note] This may take a minute. [Note] On some systems there may be some compiler warnings that can be safely ignored. Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'normalize' is not available or its output type is unknown. This occurred for: model_norm_biasvec[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1)] <<- normalize(x=model_biasvec[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1)],y=model_total[1]) This was part of the call: { model_norm_biasvec[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1)] <<- normalize(x=model_biasvec[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1)],y=model_total[1]) }"
I have tried changing this "normalizing" function from outputting a nimvector to now a scalar double, however it does not seem to be the problem here. Any suggestions please? I have attached a very simplified example of my current code and my goal to normalize a vector given in data.

###   NIMBLE Functions   ###
#_________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
library(nimble)

normalize<-nimbleFunction( #function to normalize vector
  run = function(x = double(0),y=double(0)){
    return(x / y) # Normalize to proportions
    returnType(double(0))})


###  Bugs Code  ###
#_________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

bugcode1<-nimbleCode({ #Bugs Nimble Code
  #########  Priors   ########
 
  ####### Likelihood of Data   #######
  #Likelihood of Sampling Each Class of K_Periods (as probabilities)
  total <- sum(biasvec[1:5])
  for (vec in 1:5){
    norm_biasvec[vec] <- normalize(x=biasvec[vec],y=total) }
    One ~ dbern(norm_biasvec[Class_k]) #1(k=0)/2(k=1)/3(k=2-50)/4(k=51-89)/5(k=90-99 and Inf)
 
}) #End of Bugs Code
#_________________________________________________________________________________________________________________



#3. Data
Data = list(
  Class_k = 5, #example, in my actual code, this is a vector with numbers 1:5
  One = 1,
  biasvec = c(0.01,0.1,30,40,40) #1(k=0)/2(k=1)/3(k=2-50)/4(k=51-89)/5(k=90-99 and Inf)
)
   #this is for my bugs nimble code

#5. Convert Nimble code to a Nimble Model
model1<-nimbleModel(bugcode1,data = Data, debug=F)

#6. Compile Nimble Model
compiled_model = compileNimble(model1, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

Thank you in advance!
Regards,
Cherie

messages.subject: Re: rror: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'x' is not available or its output type is unknown.
parts:
Hi Cherie,
Thanks for the question. This one is frustrating as it arises from a kind of name clash we try somewhat to protect against (but didn't here) and would have been hard for you to guess. The problem is that "normalize" is a function in the igraph package, and the search for a "normalize" to use during compileNimble is finding that one instead of the nimbleFunction you defined. Hence, your code works for me simply with a different name than "normalize". I'm going to file an issue on this. At the very least, we could revise the error message to point out this kind of potential glitch.
Perry
